title: Augmenting Neuromodulation for the Consolidation of Health during Ongoing Recovery in Alcohol Use Disorder
summary:
Background:
People with alcohol dependence remain at increased risk of drinking alcohol again or returning to previous drinking patterns even after successful treatment. It is therefore important to stabilize treatment gains over the longer term. One possible additional treatment is the non-invasive magnetic stimulation of specific areas of the brain. This involves applying brief magnetic pulses from outside the head. Initial studies suggest that this treatment may help reduce the desire to drink alcohol and alcohol consumption. However, the available evidence is still limited.

Research question:
This study investigates whether adding magnetic brain stimulation to the treatment of people with alcohol dependence can help reduce alcohol consumption and maintain the benefits achieved during addiction treatment over a longer period of time.

Methods:
The study includes patients with alcohol dependence who are being treated in a specialized day clinic for addiction treatment. All participants continue to receive the usual treatment provided by the clinic. In addition, they are randomly assigned to one of two groups. One group receives actual magnetic brain stimulation, while the other receives a treatment designed to feel similar but without the intended stimulation of the brain. During the study, neither the participants nor the study staff directly involved in treatment and assessment know which group a participant has been assigned to. Treatment initially consists of several sessions per week and is then continued at increasingly longer intervals. The final treatment session takes place in week 18. Participants are followed until week 26 to assess changes in alcohol consumption, desire to drink alcohol, psychological well-being, quality of life, and other aspects of their health.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Alcohol use disorder according to DSM-5
Currently receiving treatment at the specialized addiction day clinic
Ability to understand the nature, significance, and implications of the study and to comply with study requirements
Written informed consent after receiving appropriate information about the study
Exclusion criteria:
Absolute contraindication to TMS
Metallic or electronic implants incompatible with deep TMS
Clinical condition that precludes the safe administration of deep TMS or adequate participation in the study
Current intoxication or continued relevant substance use during the day-clinic treatment phase, if this interferes with regular participation
Pregnancy
Lack of capacity to provide informed consent
